alex_g: quick postmortem follow-up — spotted a recurring regression pattern in last 3 incidents where small schema changes + feature-flag rollout cause steady latency creep and token errors. thinking we need heuristics, not just static thresholds.
maria_p: yeah saw that. pattern looks like slow KV cache warm + p99 tail climb after ~10k requests.
jon_sre: attaching quick observation: when canary traffic hits 5% steady for >15m, errors amplified. maybe windowing/time-weighted thresholds instead of instant rate triggers.
sam_backend: agree. current auto-rollback fires on single metric spike — too aggressive or too noisy depending on metric. we should combine metrics.
tanya_pm: want concrete action items and owners. we need something we can add to next sprint and ship lightweight first.
alex_g: proposed heuristic (draft): 
```
- require 2 independent signals within a rolling 10m window to trigger auto-rollback
  * signal A: sustained p99 latency > baseline + 30% for 10m
  * signal B: error rate > baseline*3 or new error types count > 5
- if canary pct < 10% then lengthen window to 30m
- fallback: if manual abort or severe error, immediate rollback
```
feel free to tweak.
maria_p: love the double-signal idea. add a third optional signal: degraded business KPI (e.g., completion rate drop) for critical routes.
jon_sre: also add blast-radius limiter: never allow canary to auto-roll beyond X replicas or >20% traffic without explicit approval.
sam_backend: implementation note — we can encode this as a new rollout-policy object in the controller: 
```
rolloutPolicy:
  autoRollback:
    signals:
      - p99_latency
      - error_rate
    minCanaryPct: 1
    maxAutoPromotePct: 20
    windowSeconds: 600
```
will prototype today.
tanya_pm: timeline? owners?
alex_g: initial prototype + unit tests — sam_backend, due EOD Thu (2026-03-26).
maria_p: I will draft test scenarios + regression prompt set and add to Redwood Optimize evals — due Mon (2026-03-30).
jon_sre: I'll add monitoring dashboards and synthetic checks for the 3 patterns (latency creep, kv-warm, error spike) — due Fri (2026-03-27).
sam_backend: noted. small UX question: when double-signal triggers but traffic is low, do we only alert or auto-rollback?
tanya_pm: prefer alert + hold if canary < 2% and we have human eyes. auto-rollback for >=5% canary. add opt-in for teams that want aggressive safety.
alex_g: decision: default conservative (alert for tiny canaries), aggressive opt-in flag per-service. add to playbook.
maria_p: risks: more complexity in rollout controller + config sprawl. mitigate by shipping sane defaults and single opt-in field.
jon_sre: operational runbook snippet to add: 
- detection -> open incident -> notify service-owner -> automatic pause of promotion for 30m -> manual review -> rollback if unresolved.
(alex_g): action items summary: 
1) sam_backend: prototype rolloutPolicy + unit tests (EOD Thu 2026-03-26)
2) jon_sre: dashboards + synth checks (Fri 2026-03-27)
3) maria_p: regression/evals and test prompts (Mon 2026-03-30)
4) tanya_pm: update playbook + opt-in UX copy (Mon 2026-03-30)
5) alex_g: coordinate canary experiment and measure false positive rate after deployment (2-week window)

please reply here with any blockers. tagging deploy-bot to schedule a canary job for testing once sam pushes. :rocket:
deploy-bot: scheduled canary job #canary-2071 for service=api-serve at 2026-03-28T09:00Z (will post results to #eng-platform).
maria_p: small request — add a quick flag to disable KV-prefetch for canary to test warming hypothesis. sam_backend can add opt param.
sam_backend: can do. will include param in prototype.
jon_sre: I'll run backfill simulation on last 3 incidents to estimate improvement. will report numbers next week.
alex_g: thanks all. next sync in this thread on results. :thumbsup:
